scientific_status: evidence-informed stylized conifer architectural concept; not an identified extinct species
artistic_choices: Seven-meter scale, crown spacing, small asymmetry and color are original design choices.

Each spray uses five pairs and one terminal shallow lanceolate needle group. They are enlarged gallery-scale abstractions, not measured leaves or a named fossil taxon. Modern Metasequoia provides the flattened linear foliage analogue; paired grouping, taper and dimensions are artistic.
Tubular bough bases flare into and are buried within the parent trunk; intentional closed-component intersections.
provenance: Original procedural geometry. References consulted only; no external mesh or image incorporated.
source_vertex_count_convention: Sum of authored mesh vertices across unique included meshes, before modifiers; no instances or modifiers.
topology_notes: Foliage uses closed shallow six-vertex blades with paired spread, width-to-length 0.30 and thickness-to-width 0.13; foliage shares smooth normals and wood retains deliberate flat normals. All elements closed and opaque. Deliberate buried intersections at organic branch joins. No thick round foliage tubes or radial starburst clumps. Woody geometry and branchlet placements are inherited unchanged from r12. Two green palette groups follow older and younger shoot zones.

description.en: An original seven-meter conifer concept with open crown gaps, curved tapering boughs, shallow paired linear needle groups on tapered branchlet fans.
